transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello. Well... my wife thought I should come talk to someone. 

I guess I've just been... getting a bit stuck on things lately. Just checking the same boxes, or lists... looking in the condo drawers over and over before I can move on to whatever I'm doing. 

I know perfectly well I already looked, it's just... well, she gets tired of waiting for me to just leave it be. So, here I am.
Do you feel like you have to check those boxes or lists in a specific way or order?
Not really. I don't... I don't think there's any special order to it. I just look at them. That's about it.
Do you have any thoughts that keep repeating in your mind?

Well... I suppose so. Just... nagging things, mostly. 

Like worrying I might have accidentally thrown out something important from my old teaching files. Or maybe I put a tool in the wrong box. I tell myself it's highly unlikely, but... the thought just sort of sticks around. Makes it a bit hard to just sit and settle down. That's about it.
Do you ever feel like you have to check those things to prevent something bad from happening?
No, not really. I don't... I don't think anything terrible is going to happen. I just... I just feel like I need to be sure, I guess. That's all.
Do you feel like you have to perform any specific rituals or actions when you're checking these things?
No... no rituals or anything like that. I just... I just look in the boxes. Nothing special.
How much do these thoughts and checking behaviors interfere with your daily life?

Not too much, I suppose. It just... slows things down a bit. 

Unpacking the condo has taken much longer than it probably should. And... well, I've put off preparing for my library tutoring. My hobbies, too. I just feel like I can't really move on to those things until I'm sure things are verified enough. But... that's about it.
How upsetting or distressing are these nagging thoughts to you?

I suppose... they aren't terribly upsetting. Just a bit bothersome. I just keep getting these nagging thoughts that... well, that maybe I threw away something important from my old teaching files. Or... that I put a needed tool in the wrong box somewhere. I tell myself it's unlikely, but... the thought just comes back. It just makes it hard to settle down and relax. That's about it.
Have you felt like these thoughts and checking behaviors have caused you significant distress or problems in your relationships or daily activities?

Well... like I mentioned just a moment ago, it mostly just affects my own routine. The unpacking at the condo is taking much longer than it should. And... I keep putting off preparing for my library tutoring, and my hobbies. I just feel like I can't really move on to those things until I'm sure everything is verified enough. 

But as far as relationships or significant distress... no, I wouldn't say that. It's just... getting in the way of my own tasks a bit.
Would you say that these nagging thoughts and checking behaviors are causing you a lot of anxiety or discomfort?

No, not a lot. I... I wouldn't really call it anxiety. It's mostly just a nuisance. 

I don't feel panicked or anything like that. It's just... mildly unsettling until I can look over the boxes again. That's really all it is.
Do you feel like you're doing these checks because you feel compelled to, rather than just because you want to make sure?

Well... I suppose it's hard to say for sure. I just... I find myself checking the same boxes and lists over and over. The drawers here at the condo, too. 

I know perfectly well I already looked. And... well, my wife is usually waiting for me, telling me to just leave it be. But I still feel like I have to do it before I can move on to the next thing. So... yes, I guess I do feel a need to do it. That's really what brought me in.
Have you considered that you might be able to stop checking the boxes and lists if you wanted to, or do you feel like you couldn't stop even if you tried?

Well... like I just said a moment ago, that's really what brought me in. I know perfectly well I've already looked at those same boxes and lists. My wife will be waiting, telling me to just leave it be, but... I still end up checking the condo drawers again anyway. I just can't seem to move on until I do. So... I suppose I haven't been able to just stop, even when I want to.
Would you say that these checking behaviors and nagging thoughts are causing you more than minor distress?
No, I wouldn't say so. Like I mentioned before... it's just a nuisance. It's mildly unsettling, but... no, not distress. Just... bothersome.
Do you think you could be doing these checks even if you didn't feel unsettled or bothered by the thoughts?

I don't really know. It's hard to say what I'd do otherwise. 

Like I've been saying... I just find myself going through the same boxes and condo drawers over and over. I know perfectly well I already looked. My wife is waiting for me to just leave it be, but... I do it anyway, before I can move on. I'm not sure about the rest of it. That's just what happens.
Do you think these thoughts and checking behaviors are aimed at preventing something from happening, even if it's not something that you're consciously worried about?

I... I'm really not sure about preventing anything. I don't think about it like that. Like I said, it's just... I find myself checking those boxes, the lists, the drawers. Over and over. Even when I know I've looked, and my wife is standing right there waiting. I just... have to do it before I can move on. That's all it is.
Have you noticed any impact on your relationships with friends or family members due to these checking behaviors and nagging thoughts?

I wouldn't say it's a big issue with people. My wife just... waits, like I said. But it does slow everything down. Unpacking the condo has taken much longer than it should. And... well, I've been putting off my preparation for the library tutoring I do. And my hobbies. 

I just... I feel like I can't move on to those things until I've verified things enough. So it just gets in the way of getting things done, I suppose. That's about it.
Do you feel like these checking behaviors are something you can control, or do they feel somewhat automatic?

I don't really know. I haven't thought about it in those terms. 

I just... do it. Like I said, I find myself checking the boxes and the drawers. I wouldn't know if you'd call that automatic or not. It's just what happens.
Do you think you check the boxes and lists because you're afraid of making a mistake if you don't?

I don't... I wouldn't say I'm afraid. I don't really feel fear about it. 

It's just... I just have to look. I don't know why. I just look at them, and then I look again. I don't think about mistakes.
Do you feel like the way you check the boxes and lists has to be just right or symmetrical in some way?

No, it's not about that. 

I just... I just look at them. It doesn't have to be a certain way, or... symmetrical. I just have to check them. That's all.
Would you say that these checking behaviors and nagging thoughts are causing you significant distress?

Distress? No, I... I wouldn't use that word. 

It's not really upsetting or anything like that. I just... do what I have to do and move on. It doesn't really bother me all that much. It's just a thing I do.
Have you had to turn down social invitations or work opportunities because of your need to check things?

Not really. I don't... turn things down. 

It's just that things take a bit of time. Unpacking the condo, for instance... it's taken much longer than it probably should. And I suppose I've been putting off getting ready for my library tutoring. Some hobbies, too. 

I just... I feel like I can't really move on to those things until what I'm looking at is verified enough. But I'm not turning people down. It just takes a while.
